h: From Franschhoek, for Franschhoek.

t: Franschhoek welcomes visitors from around the world, yet many young people who grow up in the Valley never get the chance to study or build a career. Until 2018, anyone who wanted hospitality training had to travel to Stellenbosch or Paarl, an extra barrier that kept many talented young people out.
h: Our story · From Franschhoek, for Franschhoek.

t: It started with a simple question. Co-founder Michaela Julian was talking to a fellow guesthouse owner about where they could train their staff, and when they asked local businesses whether they needed trained staff, the answer was a resounding yes. So in 2018 Michaela Julian, Tarryn Corlett and Brian Moor opened the Academy, to give young people aged 18 to 35 from the Valley a chance they might never otherwise get.
h: Our story · From Franschhoek, for Franschhoek.

t: Today we're a registered charitable trust, and our donors make it all possible. Your support gives young people practical training, life skills and real work experience. 150 of our 156 graduates are now in full-time work, and every job helps support a whole family.
h: Our story · From Franschhoek, for Franschhoek.

t: We believe hospitality can change lives, strengthen families and transform communities. Here's how your support makes that happen.
h: More than training · Every great journey begins with an opportunity.

t: A pathway to a better future We don't just help young people find a first job. Through technical skills, discipline, values and confidence, our students learn to stay employed, grow into leadership and build careers that last. Every graduate means more financial security for a family, and a ripple effect through the community.
h: More than training · Every great journey begins with an opportunity.

t: Hospitality as a career of choice For many young people, hospitality isn't seen as a real career. We're changing that. From food and beverage service, cooking and housekeeping to reception, wine, barista skills, marketing and entrepreneurship, our students discover how far this industry can take them.
h: More than training · Every great journey begins with an opportunity.

t: Stronger businesses, stronger communities We work hand in hand with local hotels, restaurants and wine estates. Businesses gain skilled, emerging talent, graduates gain the chance to build their futures, and the Cape Winelands economy grows stronger, one employed young person at a time.
h: More than training · Every great journey begins with an opportunity.

t: The best of Franschhoek hospitality Franschhoek welcomes visitors from around the world, and every one of them is shaped by the people who greet them. Our graduates bring warmth, professionalism and genuine care, so every guest feels welcome, valued and special.

t: The people behind the Academy.
h: The people behind the Academy.

t: Michaela Julian Founder & Trustee After a decade in Asia in senior roles, my family and I settled in Franschhoek in 2016, revitalising The Corner House Guesthouse. With a background in Tourism & Management from Austria and extensive experience across luxury hotels and business services worldwide, I've focused on enhancing our guesthouse. My husband, a creative in photography and videography, and I share a passion for training and development, aiming to uplift our community through education and employment opportunities, fulfilling our dream of making a positive impact.
h: Our team · The people behind the Academy.

t: Brian Moor Trustee I'm actively engaged with “Hope Through Action”, where we harness the power of sports to open doors for disadvantaged children, teaching them crucial life skills and involving them in various positive developmental activities. In parallel, my role at the Academy is deeply fulfilling; I dedicate significant effort and share my insights tirelessly. This commitment is not just about contributing; it's about weaving the fabric of success for the project, ensuring every child we reach can dream bigger and stand stronger in facing their futures.
h: Our team · The people behind the Academy.

t: Tarryn Corlett Product Manager My drive is fuelled by a deep-rooted belief in the transformative power of charitable work. I'm committed to closing the educational divide in our industry, enhancing skills, and facilitating employment through partnerships with local businesses. Offering South Africans access to globally recognised education is not just a mission; it's a privilege. The success of this model in Franschhoek could pave the way for its replication across South Africa, broadening horizons and creating opportunities in numerous communities.
h: Our team · The people behind the Academy.

t: Jeremy Davids Academy Head & Teacher I'm deeply connected to Franschhoek. I see the untapped potential here, especially among our youth, and I'm committed to bringing their talents to the forefront in hospitality and tourism. Joining the Academy to manage and train students in 2018 was an opportunity I cherish for the impact it allows me to have. My involvement with the Franschhoek Youth Forum and my past experience in hotel staff training have shaped my vision for the Academy as a beacon of excellence and hope, aiming to produce skilled, respectful and confident graduates ready to enhance our community and its appeal to visitors and locals alike.
h: Our team · The people behind the Academy.

t: Shaneill Jefthas Assistant Trainer & Logistics Coordinator I'm Shaneill Jefthas, raised in the beautiful Franschhoek Valley and a proud graduate of Groendal Secondary. After matriculation, my journey took a turn when college didn't pan out, leading me to the local retail scene before diving into the hospitality industry in 2006 at Le Quartier Français. This role was a gateway to expanding my hospitality and tourism knowledge, a path that eventually led me to Protea Hotels by Marriott, where I've been thriving as a Reservations Manager. I'm thrilled to be joining the Franschhoek Hospitality Academy, ready to share my experiences, learn, and contribute to our collective success.
h: Our team · The people behind the Academy.

t: Nicola Spilsbury Chef Lecturer Bringing my international experience and teaching background to the role of Chef Lecturer, I aim to enrich our students' learning journey with a global perspective on culinary arts. This diversity in experience not only broadens their understanding of different cuisines and techniques but also prepares them for a competitive and evolving industry. My goal is to inspire creativity, foster a passion for culinary excellence, and equip our students with the skills and confidence needed to thrive in any culinary environment worldwide.
h: Our team · The people behind the Academy.

t: Reuben Riffel Ambassador Born and bred in Franschhoek, Reuben has left an indelible mark on the culinary scene both locally and internationally. As a celebrity chef and honorary ambassador, he is committed to mentoring our students.
h: Meet Reuben Riffel · Born and bred in Franschhoek.

t: Margot Janse Ambassador Dutch-born Margot led the kitchen at Le Quartier Français in Franschhoek for more than 20 years, where she made The Tasting Room one of the world's most celebrated restaurants. She was twice named Eat Out Chef of the Year and became Africa's first Relais & Châteaux Grand Chef. In 2009 she started Isabelo, which feeds schoolchildren across the Franschhoek Valley every school day.
h: Meet Reuben Riffel · Born and bred in Franschhoek.

t: Matthew Gordon Ambassador Matthew opened his first restaurant, Le Ballon Rouge, in Franschhoek when he was just 24. He and his wife Nicky ran the Haute Cabrière Cellar restaurant for 16 years, and for a quarter of a century he ran French Connection Bistro on Franschhoek's main road. Few chefs know the Valley's kitchens better.
h: Meet Reuben Riffel · Born and bred in Franschhoek.

t: Ryan Shell Ambassador Ryan has cooked in leading restaurants in the UK and at five-star properties across southern Africa, and worked under Margot Janse at Le Quartier Français. After lecturing at the Prue Leith Chefs Academy he took over the kitchen at Haute Cabrière. Today he is the chef behind Eleven, Ōku and Yama in Franschhoek, where some of our graduates now work.

h: Two graduates a year go on to study in Austria.

t: Every year since our first class in 2018, our top graduates have won full scholarships to ITM College in Austria. They study for two years in English, train in a live hotel and earn an Austrian State Diploma. In 2026 Dillon Samuels and Jason Williams became our latest ITM graduates.

t: Questions students ask us.
h: Questions students ask us.

t: How do I apply? Fill in the application form at the bottom of this page. If you're shortlisted, we'll invite you for an interview. If you're accepted, pay the R1,400 deposit by 31 December 2026 to secure your place. Applications for 2027 close on 30 October 2026.
h: FAQ · Questions students ask us.

t: Who can apply? Young people aged 18 to 35. You'll need Grade 12 with at least a 50% average, but we keep six places each year for applicants who don't have Grade 12 but do have years of work experience.
h: FAQ · Questions students ask us.

t: Do I need hospitality experience? No. You don't need any experience. We'll teach you everything you need.
h: FAQ · Questions students ask us.

t: How many students do you take? We take 26 students a year.
h: FAQ · Questions students ask us.
q: How many students do you take?

t: What are the fees? For 2027 there is a once-off registration fee of R2,800 if you're selected: a R1,400 deposit by 31 December 2026 and R1,400 on the first day, 11 January 2027. Monthly school fees are R1,400, due on the 7th of each month.
h: FAQ · Questions students ask us.

t: Is there help with fees? Unfortunately we can't help with fees, so please make sure you and your family can cover them before you apply. You'll find the full fees above.
h: FAQ · Questions students ask us.

t: Where is the Academy? Our main campus is on Farm Cabrière, Daniel Hugo Street, Franschhoek. We also have a satellite campus in Prince Albert with the Prince Albert Community Trust.
h: FAQ · Questions students ask us.

t: How long is the course? Nine months of theory and practical training at the Academy, from January to September. Then a four-month work placement from October to January, putting your training to work in a real business.
h: FAQ · Questions students ask us.

t: What will I learn? Food & beverage service, wine fundamentals, hotel reception, housekeeping, cooking theory and practical cooking, coffee & barista training, life skills & leadership, Franschhoek concierge, online booking systems, entrepreneurship, social media & personal branding, an introduction to South African brandy, and Lobster Ink online learning.
h: FAQ · Questions students ask us.

t: Who can I speak to? Call or WhatsApp Shaneill on 081 009 5157 , or email shaneill@franschhoekhospitalityacademy.co.za .

h: Our training comes to the Karoo through a partnership in Prince Albert
p: Our training comes to the Karoo through a partnership in Prince Albert

t: A new hospitality academy in the Karoo, bringing the same standard of training our students receive in Franschhoek to young people in Prince Albert.
h: ← All Diary posts Partners · December 2025 · Our training comes to the Karoo through a partnership in Prince Albert
p: Our training comes to the Karoo through a partnership in Prince Albert

t: In a significant stride towards enhancing hospitality education in South Africa, the Franschhoek Hospitality Academy & Learning Centre (FHA) has announced a formal partnership with the Prince Albert Community Trust (PACT). This collaboration will give rise to the Prince Albert Community Trust Hospitality Academy (PACTHA), a new campus set to operate in Prince Albert, mirroring the high educational standards of the FHA.
h: ← All Diary posts Partners · December 2025 · Our training comes to the Karoo through a partnership in Prince Albert
p: Our training comes to the Karoo through a partnership in Prince Albert

t: The establishment of PACTHA signals not just an educational milestone, but a pivotal moment for the local community, aimed at uplifting the lives of historically disadvantaged youth. By bringing premium hospitality training to rural areas, this initiative is poised to change lives, create job opportunities and strengthen local economies, a vision echoed fervently by PACT's founder, Ingrid Wolfaardt.

t: As part of their ongoing Beverage Training, our students recently had the incredible opportunity to visit Oldenburg Vineyards and Cape Brewing Company, gaining valuable first-hand exposure to two of South Africa's exciting beverage industries.
h: ← All Diary posts Monthly update · October 2026 · Beverage training at Oldenburg Vineyards and Cape Brewing Company
p: Beverage training at Oldenburg Vineyards and Cape Brewing Company

t: These educational excursions are about so much more than simply tasting wine and beer. They give our students the opportunity to see, experience and understand the industry from the inside: from production and presentation to service, tasting and the guest experience.
